Marissa — thanks for the summary and the draft MAP. A few clarifications from our end after reviewing with our compliance team:

1) PHI handling: We will be sending identifiable PHI during the pilot for validation (names, MRNs). We expect Redwood to support:
   - In-transit encryption (TLS 1.2+),
   - At-rest encryption with customer-managed keys (KMS),
   - Option to redact or pseudonymize in the pipeline if requested.

2) Retention: Our policy requires that raw inputs containing PHI be retained for no more than 30 days unless specifically approved; structured outputs (summaries with PHI removed) can be retained longer (up to 2 years). We also need clear deletion workflows on request.

3) Logging & audit trails: We need request-level audit logs (requestor identity, timestamp, model variant used, response hash) retained for at least 1 year, searchable by request ID.

Yes please loop in your Security/SEs — Marcus and Dev would be helpful. Also cc'ing our clinical lead, Dr. Rajesh Kumar (he may join the technical call).

—
Sarah Nguyen
Head of Data & Compliance | HealthTech.ai
sarah@healthtech.ai

Hi Sarah — looping in some technical clarifications and an updated milestones spreadsheet (redwood_map_milestones_v1.xlsx). I focused the Data Handling milestone on responsibilities and dependencies. Key notes: 

- Ingestion path: We support both client-side pseudonymization and direct ingestion. If PHI is sent directly, we recommend enabling KV/prefix caching only for non-PHI fields and disabling persistent raw input storage.
- Encryption: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for at-rest encryption. We can provide key rotation logs that align with your audit requirements.
- Audit logs & searchability: Our request logs capture request ID, timestamp, route/model variant, token usage, and requestor (when using API keys or OAuth). Logs can be exported to your SIEM (S3/CloudWatch) and retained per your policy.
- Deletion: We support an automated deletion workflow via an API call and Grafana/console controls. Deletions generate a deletion-event with timestamp and operator.

Responsibilities (proposed in MAP):
- HealthTech.ai: confirm pseudonymization approach (+ provide sample payloads), indicate retention windows, provide approved list of PHI fields.
- Redwood Inference: implement KMS-backed encryption, enable request-level audit logging to HealthTech.ai's SIEM, expose deletion workflow, and document cipher suites and compliance artifacts.

Dependencies:
- SOC 2 evidence (we attached a SOC2-SLA-summary.pdf) and a short security questionnaire will be required before we enable production keys.

I've attached the milestones spreadsheet with suggested target dates and owners. Happy to run a 30-min technical sync next week.

Subject: Re: MAP draft - Data handling & compliance requirements (security details)

Sarah — quick note from Security. We appreciate the retention windows you shared; here are how we can meet them and what we need from you: 

- Encryption & KMS: We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS / GCP KMS. We will need the KMS key ARN and a brief IAM role/trust setup for cross-account access during provisioning.
- PHI/PII handling: For pilot, we can enable an ingestion-only endpoint that keeps raw inputs for up to 30 days (configurable) and automatically triggers the deletion API. For long-term storage of derived outputs, we will use a separate locked S3 bucket with restricted access.
- Logging & audit trails: Request logs will include: request_id, api_key_id, caller_identity (if using OAuth), model_version, timestamp, and a response_hash. We can send logs to your SIEM and set a retention policy of 1 year. Note: log content will avoid storing full raw inputs by default; raw inputs are stored only if pilot mode is turned on.
- PHI-specific constraints: We recommend using field-level pseudonymization for any credit-card-like or identifier fields. If you need HIPAA BAA-level assurances, we'll need to escalate contracting (BAA addendum) — proposed milestone in MAP to finalize BAA by 2026-02-25.

What we need from HealthTech.ai:
- Confirmation on pilot mode (raw inputs enabled for up to 30 days) vs pseudonymization only.
- KMS key ARN or decision to use Redwood-managed keys for pilot.
- Any specific SIEM endpoints or log format requirements.

I attached the SOC2 summary for quick reference. Happy to join the technical sync.

—
Dev Patel
Security & Compliance Engineer | Redwood Inference
